problems.title: A quotient of three-angle sums
problems.question: Simplify $(\sin2a-\sin3a+\sin4a)/(\cos2a-\cos3a+\cos4a)$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Sum-to-product gives numerator $\sin3a(2\cos a-1)$ and denominator $\cos3a(2\cos a-1)$.
steps: On the original nonzero-denominator domain, the shared factor cancels.

problems.title: Count roots over a full revolution
problems.question: How many roots has $\sin2x=\cos x$ on[0,2π]?
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: $\sin2x-\cos x=\cos x(2\sin x-1)$.
steps: cos x=0 gives x=π/2,3π/2. sin x=1/2 gives x=π/6,5π/6. They are distinct and neither endpoint is a root.

problems.title: Symmetry of binomial coefficients
problems.question: Evaluate $\binom{12}7/\binom{12}5$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: $\binom nk=\binom n{n-k}$.
steps: Since 12−7=5, the numerator and denominator are equal and nonzero.

problems.title: Height of a square frustum
problems.question: A regular square frustum has base sides 10,4 and lateral edge 5. Find its height.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The horizontal projection of a lateral edge has coordinate offsets 3,3, so its squared length is 18.
steps: The right-triangle relation gives h²=5²−18=7.

problems.title: Equal sum and difference lengths
problems.question: Nonzero vectors a, b satisfy |a+b|=|a−b|. Find their angle.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Squaring and subtracting gives $4a\cdot b=0$.
steps: Because both vectors are nonzero, the zero dot product means their angle is 90°.

problems.title: A shifted sine cancels two cosines
problems.question: Evaluate $\sin(2a-3\pi/2)+\cos(2a-8\pi/3)+\cos(2a+2\pi/3)$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The sine is cos 2a. Reduce the second cosine’s phase modulo 2π, then sum the two cosines.
steps: They become cos(2a−2π/3)+cos(2a+2π/3)=2cos2a cos(2π/3)=−cos 2a. Add cos 2a to cancel.

problems.title: Square a strict radical inequality
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{x+1}<x-1$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The right side must be positive, so x>1. Squaring then preserves the inequality.
steps: x+1<(x−1)² gives x²−3x>0, or x(x−3)>0. With x>1, this means x>3. Every such x meets the original domain.

problems.title: Conditional probability for two odd dice
problems.question: Given both fair dice show odd numbers, find the probability their sum exceeds 8.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The conditioned outcomes are the 9 equally likely pairs from{1,3,5}².
steps: Only(5,5) has sum greater than 8.

problems.title: Common period of two frequencies
problems.question: Find the least positive period of $\sin(2x+\pi/3)+\cos(3x-\pi/4)$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: A common period must satisfy $2T=2\pi m$ and $3T=2\pi n$ for integers m, n.
steps: The distinct nonzero frequencies cannot cancel under a shift. Since 2 and 3 are coprime, the least positive common period is 2π.

problems.title: Integer points in a radical-inverse domain
problems.question: How many integers belong to the domain of $\sqrt{\sin x}/\arcsin(x-4)$?
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The inverse sine requires 3≤x≤5, and its denominator excludes x=4. The radical requires sin x≥0.
steps: The integer candidates are 3,4,5. The value 3 has positive sine;4 is excluded;5 has negative sine. Thus only 3 works.

problems.title: Area from a sine and a dot product
problems.question: In ABC, sin B=1/3 and BA·BC=16√2. Find are a.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The positive dot product implies cos B>0, so $\cos B=2\sqrt2/3$. Then $AB\cdot BC=16\sqrt2/\cos B=24$.
steps: The triangle are a is(1/2)AB·BC·sin B=(1/2)·24/3.

problems.title: Two perpendicular slants to a plane
problems.question: A point is h above a plane. Two segments from it meet the plane at angle φ and are perpendicular to each other. Find the distance between their feet.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Both slant lengths are $l=h/\sin\varphi$. The two segments for m equal perpendicular legs of a right triangle.
steps: The foot-to-foot distance is √(l²+l²)=√2l.

problems.title: A vector identity for all vectors
problems.question: Which printed equality holds for all vectors a, b?
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The dot product is distributive and symmetric. Thus $(a+b)\cdot(a-b)=|a|^2-|b|^2$.
steps: Expanding yields |a|²−a·b+b·a−|b|². The mixed terms cancel. The other offered squared-product identities fail in general or confuse scalar and vector products.

problems.title: Three dot products in a right triangle
problems.question: ABC is right at C with hypotenuse 5. Find AB·AC+BC·BA+CA·CB.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Take C as origin, A=u, B=v, with u·v=0.
steps: AB·AC=(v−u)·(−u)=|u|². BC·BA=(−v)·(u−v)=|v|². CA·CB=u·v=0. Their sum is the hypotenuse squared.

problems.title: Maximum of a cosine quadratic
problems.question: Find max $5\cos^2x-6\cos x+2$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Put t=cos x∈[−1,1]. The quadratic 5t²−6t+2 is convex, so its maximum on this interval occurs at an endpoint.
steps: At t=−1 its value is 13; at t=1 it is 1. Both endpoint cosine values are attained.

problems.title: Locate an inverse-trigonometric value
problems.question: Which printed interval contains $\arccos(\sin(-2\pi/9))$?
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The inner sine is −sin 40°=cos 130°. Since 130° lies in the principal arccos range[0°,180°], the inverse value is 130°.
steps: It lies between 120° and 135°, equivalently 2π/3 and 3π/4.

problems.title: A homothety coordinate
problems.question: B=(x−1,−3) is the image of A=(3,3) under a homothety centred at M=(1,1). Find x.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
steps: The second coordinate gives k=−2. Then x−2=−4.

problems.title: Equality at a trigonometric amplitude
problems.question: 20sin2a+21cos2a=29. Find cot a.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The coefficient amplitude is $\sqrt{20^2+21^2}=29$. Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz forces sin 2a=20/29, cos 2a=21/29.
steps: Use cot a=(1+cos 2a)/sin 2a=(50/29)/(20/29). The sine is nonzero, so the quotient is valid.

problems.title: Probability of a radical inequality
problems.question: Uniformly choose x∈[−5,5]. Find the chance $\sqrt{2x+8}\ge x$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: The domain is x≥−4. For−4≤x≤0, the right side is nonpositive, so the inequality holds.
steps: For x>0, square to get x²−2x−8≤0, or −2≤x≤4. Combining with x>0 adds(0,4]. The favourable interval is[−4,4], length 8, out of 10.

problems.title: Count all face diagonals of a prism
problems.question: A prism has 20 diagonals lying in its faces. Find its edge count.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: For an n-gonal prism, the lateral faces contribute 2n diagonals and the two bases contribute n(n−3). Total is n(n−1).
steps: Solve n(n−1)=20 to get n=5. The edge count is 3n.

problems.title: Surface area of a tri-rectangular tetrahedron
problems.question: A pyramid has right-triangle base with legs 1,2, and height 3 rising from the right-angle vertex. Find total surface are a.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
steps: Three mutually perpendicular coordinate-plane faces have areas 1,3/2,3. The remaining face SAB has are a half |(B−A)×(S−A)|. The cross product is(6,3,2), length 7, so its are a is 7/2.

problems.title: Unit direction of an internal bisector
problems.question: OA=(6,8), OB=(5,12). Find the unit vector codirected with the internal bisector OC.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Add the two unit side directions: $OA/10+OB/13=(64/65,112/65)=(16/65)(4,7)$.
steps: The internal bisector points in this sum’s direction. Normalise(4,7), whose length is √65.

problems.title: A disguised tangent subtraction
problems.question: Solve $\tan x=[2-(1+\tan13°)^2]/[2-(1-\tan13°)^2]$.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Put t=tan 13°. The quotient is $(1-2t-t^2)/(1+2t-t^2)$. Dividing by 1−t² gives $(1-\tan26°)/(1+\tan26°)$.
steps: This is tan(45°−26°)=tan 19°. Tangent has period 180°.

problems.title: Range of an absolute trigonometric quadratic
problems.question: For which a does $|5\sin^2x+\cos x-7|=a$ have a solution?
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Put c=cos x∈[−1,1]. The inner expression is −5c²+c−2, always negative, since its maximum is −39/20. Thus the absolute value is 5c²−c+2.
steps: Complete the square:5(c−1/10)²+39/20, whose minimum 39/20 is attained. Its maximum on[−1,1] is at c=−1, with value 8. Continuity supplies all intermediate values.

problems.title: Two diagonal sections of an oblique parallelepiped
problems.question: A parallelepiped has square base, and its lateral edge makes 60° with both adjacent base sides. Find are a AA₁C₁C divided by are a BB₁D₁D.
problems.idea: Apply an exact identity or model and retain the original domain.
formulas: Let adjacent base vectors u, v have length a and be perpendicular, and lateral vector w have length l. Then $w\cdot u=w\cdot v=al/2$.
steps: The first diagonal is u+v, length a√2, and its dot product with w is al. Thus its angle to w has cosine 1/√2 and sine 1/√2. The first section are a is a√2·l/√2=al.
The other diagonal is v−u, length a√2, and is perpendicular to w because their dot product vanishes. Its section are a is a√2l. Divide.
